## About the company

Smallest.ai builds voice AI for real-world conversations. We work across the entire voice stack, from understanding speech to generating natural responses, and give businesses the tools to run it reliably at scale. Today, our technology handles millions of call minutes every month.

## Meet our founders

Smallest.ai was founded by Sudarshan Kamath and Akshat Mandloi. Before starting the company, they worked together on Bosch’s autonomous vehicles team, building systems where speed and reliability really mattered. That experience shaped a simple idea: smaller, focused AI models can often do a better job in the real world.

## General instructions

These guidelines help partners, customers, press, and community members represent smallest.ai clearly and consistently. Use the assets provided here without modifying their proportions, colours, or composition.

## Logo spacing

Clearance ensures the legibility and impact of the smallest.ai logo by separating it from surrounding visual elements. This protected space should be treated as the minimum safe area around the logo, though wherever possible, additional breathing room is encouraged to maintain clarity and presence.

For smallest.ai, the clearance area is measured using the height of the “m” in the wordmark. This unit should be maintained consistently on all sides of the logo.

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/EqwgWhzVuZ7r3gDtsOJU7bStCI4.png?width=1020&height=494)

![](https://framerusercontent.com/images/Sp8z9Sx3YkzpWqmYMeeQRRJX4.png?width=1020&height=492)

## Logo misuse

To keep our identity clear and consistent, always use the Smallest AI logo exactly as provided. Do not alter its opacity, add effects or outlines, change its spacing, rearrange its elements, or distort its proportions.

![Opacity logo misuse example](https://framerusercontent.com/images/PHGjsi8kYV1EKgxpbMLkCYkWTg.png?width=560&height=427)

Opacity

Avoid lowering the opacity or making the logo transparent. The logo should remain fully visible to preserve readability.

![Drop Shadow logo misuse example](https://framerusercontent.com/images/DQJnRWycu20MMjkYU4dCI2s6FZk.png?width=560&height=427)

Drop Shadow

Avoid applying shadows, glows, bevels, gradients, or other visual effects to the logo. Keep the logo flat, clean, and minimal.

![Outline logo misuse example](https://framerusercontent.com/images/KJ7W31i9LwKMrYKeTSxlypvI6ZM.png?width=560&height=427)

Outline

Do not apply strokes or outlines around the logo or typography. The logo should never appear with decorative borders or effects.

![Stretching logo misuse example](https://framerusercontent.com/images/9FDLtfvzUMeOV4veF54GViAouI.png?width=560&height=427)

Stretching

Never stretch, squash, or distort the logo. Always scale proportionally to maintain the integrity of the mark and typography.

![Spacing logo misuse example](https://framerusercontent.com/images/091IYJoBmpWeoWGaILRGgsSQ4.png?width=560&height=427)

Spacing

Do not modify the spacing between letters, symbols and other elements within the logo. The logo should remain untouched.

![Stacking logo misuse example](https://framerusercontent.com/images/6RFyqa9h92qpKCgHCy3gH2cg7g.png?width=560&height=427)

Stacking

Do not stack or rearrange the symbol and wordmark. Always use the approved horizontal lockup to maintain consistency.
